name: Novena
summary: Medical-hub NSL stop — hospital gravity, mid-town condo stock, and errand density without full Orchard tourist crush.
body: Novena is the shortlist when hospital-adjacent convenience and North-South Line mid-town access matter more than quiet cul-de-sac living. The Square / hospital belt concentrates clinics, food, and weekday traffic; housing is mostly condo towers with selective older stock. Expats land here for car-light hops to CBD and Orchard without paying full River Valley nightlife premiums. Watch-outs: medical traffic peaks, variable building age, and fire-alarm / detector culture that differs estate-by-estate. Compare with Newton for food-street energy, Toa Payoh Central for heartland town-centre texture, and the combined Novena–Newton entity when you want both stops in one shortlist.
bestFor: renters who will book ActiveSG mats instead of trusting condo wellness rooms
watchOuts: Variable condo age and MA responsiveness
Detector / false-alarm recovery rules differ by estate
Less café-strip cohesion than Holland V
housingMix: Mid-to-large condos; limited quiet HDB texture at the station core.
commuteNotes: North-South Line at Novena; Downtown Line nearby depending on block. Time a weekday 08:15 door-to-desk before you LOI.
